items.reply: This is by design: the spec puts --shout before the name, and other argument orders are out of scope. `greet.sh ada --shout` prints `hello ada`, the same as before the change.

finding.proof: bin/greet.sh:9 runs `echo "${line}"`, and the name comes from argv. Under macOS /bin/sh, `sh bin/greet.sh 'a\tb'` prints a real tab where the old printf printed a backslash and a t.
finding.claim: `echo` turns backslash sequences in the name into control characters on some POSIX sh builds, so names with a backslash print differently from before the change.

items.note: This is true: `tr a-z A-Z` only uppercases ASCII, and in non-C locales its ranges are unspecified. The author has limited names to ASCII, and the spec doesn't ask for more. `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'` would be the portable form if that ever changes.

items.reply: Confirmed: `sh bin/greet.sh --shout` with no name prints `HELLO WORLD`. Line 5 shifts the flag off, and `${1:-world}` then falls back safely under `set -u`.

noticed.text: The MR's only commit message is `Add --shout` and has no typo. The resolved thread about a typo matches nothing in the commit as it is now.
The tests only cover the plain greeting. Nothing checks --shout, even though the spec's done-when asks for `--shout ada` to print HELLO ADA.
